These are the events that have already occurred:

...
68. Marianne planned to travel to Savannah for advice on marriage.
69. Marianne expressed his interest in Miss Lucian Robillard.
70. Marianne was informed that Lucian's father would not approve of him as a son-in-law.
71. Marianne learned of Lucian's love for her cousin, Philippe Robillard.
72. Lucian decided to marry Marianne after a personal crisis.


Below is a list of possible subsequent events:

["Lucian's cousin quietly questioned his choice of Marianne as partner.", "Lucian's best friend secretly envied his bond with Marianne.", "Lucian's siblings openly dismissed her relationship with Marianne.", "Lucian's mother cautiously supported his decision to be with Marianne.", "Lucian's aunt unexpectedly celebrated their engagement with Marianne.", "Lucian's father reluctantly accepted her marriage to Marianne."]

 Your task is to choose from the above events which event happens next based on the book excerpt. In your response to me, only include the answer without anything else.
references: Lucian's father reluctantly accepted her marriage to Marianne.

Mother had always been just as she was, a pillar of strength, a fount of wisdom, the one person who knew the answers to everything.

But Debbie was wrong, for, years before, Lucian Robillard of Savannah had giggled as inexplicably as any fifteen-year-old in that charming coastal city and whispered the long nights through with friends, exchanging confidences, telling all secrets but one.

That was the year when Marianne O’Kerry, twenty-eight years older than she, came into her life—the year, too, when youth and her black-eyed cousin, Philippe Robillard, went out of it.

For when Philippe, with his snapping eyes and his wild ways, left Savannah forever, he took with him the glow that was in Lucian’s heart and left for the bandy-legged little Irishman who married her only a gentle shell.

But that was enough for Marianne, overwhelmed at his unbelievable luck in actually marrying her.

And if anything was gone from her, he never missed it.
